title: Crop by rows and columns
summary: Cropping selects a rectangle from an image. NumPy slices use start positions and stop just before the end positions.
introduction: Cropping selects a rectangle from an image. NumPy slices use start positions and stop just before the end positions. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain crop by rows and columns
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Cropping selects a rectangle from an image. NumPy slices use start positions and stop just before the end positions.

blocks.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np

image = np.arange(20, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(4, 5)
crop = image[1:3, 2:5].copy()
print(crop.tolist())
blocks.title: Crop by rows and columns

blocks.text: The output is [[7, 8, 9], [12, 13, 14]]. Rows 1 and 2 and columns 2, 3 and 4 are selected. copy makes a separate array.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Crop the first two rows and first two columns.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A slice can share memory with its source; use copy when you need independent pixels.
For more detail later, use this [OpenCV further reading](https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d6/d00/tutorial_py_root.html).
